sections.advice: San Antonio de los Cobres → Abra del Acay climbs about 4895 m in 32 km. This is the part worth slowing down for - look through the bends and use the pull-offs.

abra-del-acay-road.provenance: CURATED FROM THE ARCHIVE: waypoints taken from the named road Abra del Acay Road. Distances between stops are great-circle with a road factor, not a routed measurement - the pipeline replaces them when it routes this line.

scenicChapters.title: Abra del Acay Road
scenicChapters.narrative: The valley floor is behind you and the road starts working for its height at about 15.1%. Corners stack above one another where the ground allows nothing straighter — first and second gear more often than not. Look through each corner to the next one and let the engine do the holding.

scenicChapters.title: Abra del Acay → La Poma
scenicChapters.narrative: 4895 m come off over 72 km at around 12.5%. The road gives back what the climb took, faster than it took it. Brakes early, eyes far ahead. A descent this long asks more of concentration than of pace.

abra-del-acay-road.story: 234 km from San Antonio de los Cobres to Cachí, about 3 h 09 of riding. It goes by way of Abra del Acay and La Poma. The highest point is about 4,900 m. It suits an unhurried touring pace.

places-roca-del-senallo-val-del-charco-d.story: A 255 km round trip from Culla - roughly 4 h 24 in the saddle. On the way it passes Abric de la Tenalla, Val del Charco del Agua Amarga and back through Abric de la Tenalla. The highest point is about 1,250 m. It was put together for the scenery rather than the shortest line.
